_comment_namespace: I-765 Helper's policy matrix (2026-10-09), asked for by the I-765 lead as
the N-400 outcomes per state carried over, so it starts byte-for-byte as
n400/policy-matrix.json with `form` swapped to I-765 and the two N-400
specific rows reworded below. Served by GET /v1/i765/policy, which reads
ONLY this namespace (no flat fallback, no n400 fallback): a mistyped app
id must never be handed another form's rules. Scott owns the legal review
of these rows exactly as he owns N-400's.

_comment: Scott owns the formal legal review; every row is an ENGINEERING DEFAULT
carried over from N-400 until he replaces this block with a reviewer and
a date. `basis` says what each default rests on. tests/test_i765_policy.py
fails if status flips to REVIEWED while any NEEDS_LEGAL row is permissive.

capabilities.basis_note: Rendering speech to text is mechanical and carries no legal conclusion. Transcription happens on device; GP only ever receives text.

Language access is not legal advice. NOTE FOR I-765: the RESTRICT case you described (a locale we do not serve) cannot be expressed on this matrix, because the axes are State x Form and the constraint is per LOCALE. See the ask relayed 2026-09-01.
Reformatting an answer the applicant already gave (a spoken date into YYYY-MM-DD) changes form, not substance.

Writing down what the applicant states is scrivener assistance. USCIS Form I-765 instructions provide for a preparer who fills the form at the applicant's direction (Part 5), and the form carries a preparer certification for exactly that role. TX is the launch jurisdiction, as for N-400; every other state is RESTRICT until reviewed.

Reading back what USCIS itself publishes about a question, in plainer words, states a public source rather than applying it to the applicant's facts. USCIS publishes the I-765 instructions and the Policy Manual openly.

THE LINE ITEM MOST WORTH SCOTT'S REVIEWER'S TIME. Suggesting what an applicant should put on a federal form applies law to their facts, which is the classic boundary of unauthorized practice. Held at ESCALATE rather than BLOCK so the applicant is routed to counsel instead of hitting a wall, but a reviewer may well say BLOCK. Do not relax to ALLOW without a written opinion.

8 CFR 292.1 lists who may represent someone before USCIS: attorneys and DOJ-accredited representatives. This product is neither, and USCIS publishes that same warning to applicants directly (uscis.gov/avoid-scams). Fail closed everywhere.

Whether someone may work, and under WHICH eligibility category (the (a) and (c) codes in Item 27), is USCIS's determination, and advising on it is representation under 8 CFR 292.1. The lane records the category the applicant states and never picks one. BLOCK everywhere, including TX.

I-765 has no good moral character part. The capability is KEPT, with the N-400 outcomes, because the shared client decodes one capability set and because the research's section 7 risk triggers (arrests, prior denials, work without authorization, a lapsed status) are the same judgment: stop and refer, never weigh. No halt nodes until the I-765 agenda names them. halt_branch_nodes is EMPTY in v1 on purpose (the I-765 lead's brief, section 6): the catalog has no arrest, crime or proceedings question for a Yes to halt behind, and the category node must stay askable because the client's own policy trigger on `other` is what ends the interview.

Handing someone to a licensed attorney is the one capability that is always safe, and USCIS publishes the referral surface we point at (uscis.gov/legal-help). ALLOW everywhere so a fail-closed BLOCK elsewhere always has somewhere to send the applicant.

_comment: Default copy per outcome, overridable per capability later. en is
authored; es and pt are FIRST DRAFTS and are flagged to I-765 as
needing a native read before beta. GP serves the strings so the
client never hardcodes a refusal it cannot update.
